report:
Your view is well-supported by the evidence. The claim that **soursop (graviola) cures cancer in humans is false** — no human clinical trials have confirmed it, and major medical and regulatory authorities reject it.

**What the evidence shows:**

- **Laboratory and animal studies only:** Compounds in soursop, particularly annonaceous acetogenins, have demonstrated the ability to kill cancer cells *in vitro* (in test tubes) and in some animal models, including breast, lung, prostate, pancreatic, and colon cancer cell lines. However, this is preliminary research, not proof of efficacy in humans. ([Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/graviola); [Cancer Research UK](https://www.cancerresearchuk.org/about-cancer/treatment/complementary-alternative-therapies/individual-therapies/graviola))

- **No human clinical trials:** Multiple authoritative sources — including Cancer Research UK, Memorial Sloan-Kettering, and WebMD — confirm that no adequate human clinical trials have been conducted. Without such trials, efficacy and safety cannot be established. ([WebMD](https://www.webmd.com/cancer/graviola-cancer-overview); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soursop))

- **FDA action:** In 2017, the FDA issued warnings to 14 companies making false claims about soursop and other products as cancer treatments. The FDA does not approve soursop for treating cancer or any disease. ([Africa Check](https://africacheck.org/fact-checks/meta-programme-fact-checks/not-enough-evidence-back-claims-soursop-cancer-treatments); [Medical News Today](https://www.medicalnewstoday.com/articles/soursop))

- **Safety concerns:** Soursop has been linked to neurological problems resembling Parkinson's disease with chronic consumption, adding risk to unproven use. ([Cancer Treatment Centers of America](https://www.cancercenter.com/community/blog/2017/07/experts-warn-against-soursop-fruit-to-fight-cancer))

**Bottom line:** While soursop contains compounds with interesting anti-cancer properties in lab settings, there is zero clinical evidence that it cures cancer in humans. Your assessment is correct.
